text: 📈 Specialist consultations up 60% in Mexico's public health system. "In 2022 there were 19.7 million specialty consultations from January to July. This year? 31.7 million — 60 percent more, nearly 12 million additional specialty consultations." — Eduardo Clark, Deputy Health Secretary The increase tracks a policy in place since 2018: train and hire more specialists in the public sector. Up 4.5 million in the last year alone.

🩺 101 million doctor visits. A first in Mexico's history. "This year, from January to July, we surpassed 100 million for the first time in history — 101,233,444 primary care consultations. That's up 28 percent from 2022." — Eduardo Clark, Deputy Health Secretary Combined across IMSS, ISSSTE and IMSS Bienestar. In the last year alone, consultations jumped from 95 million to 101 million.

🇲🇽💰 <u>CUSTOMS COLLECTION HITS RECORD 131.6 BILLION PESOS</u>

Mexico's customs agency ANAM collected 131,616 million pesos in July — the highest monthly take of 2026 and up 5.4% from a year earlier — across nearly 1.96 million foreign trade operations, the most since January 2025. ANAM credits "greater efficiency in customs operations and stronger actions against illegal trade": for every peso it spent collecting, it brought back 400. The port of Manzanillo alone moved over 15% of the revenue. (El Financiero)

🇲🇽🚍 <u>BAJA CALIFORNIA'S MOBILITY INSTITUTE EARNS ISO 9001</u>

One year of work standardizing every procedure just paid off: Baja California's Sustainable Mobility Institute (IMOS) received ISO 9001:2025 certification, covering its offices in Tijuana, Ensenada, San Felipe, San Quintín and Mexicali — faster paperwork, fewer errors, and documented processes built to outlast any administration. Governor Marina del Pilar: "It shows that in Baja California you can have quality government, with transparency, efficiency and results that are measurable."

🇲🇽📱 <u>MEXICO ASKS 1 MILLION TEACHERS ABOUT PHONES IN CLASS</u>

Before regulating cellphones in schools nationwide, Mexico's SEP will ask the people who actually run the classrooms: over 1 million teachers in more than 200,000 schools will weigh in on August 24-25. Sixteen states already have rules. The evidence behind the push is ugly — former Meta researcher Ravi Iyer notes 70% of young people feel manipulated by the platforms, and Meta's own internal research showed 13% of Instagram users aged 13 to 15 received unwanted sexual advances in a single week.
